GreedyKS drift detector

Source: R/dfr_greedyks.R
dfr_greedyks.Rd

Online one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of a numeric stream against a reference distribution, with the GreedyKS sketch of Cardoso and Galeno (2023): a drift is signalled when the p-value of the estimated statistic falls to alpha or below. The detector is used for virtual concept drift on a numeric feature, or on the error of a model.

Usage

dfr_greedyks(
  cdf = "norm",
  m = 100,
  alpha = 0.01,
  grace_period = m,
  reference_size = 1000,
  exact = TRUE,
  min_instances = 0,
  target_feat = NULL
)

Arguments

cdf

The reference distribution: a CDF (a function of a numeric vector, kept for the whole stream), or one of "norm", "exp" and "unif", whose parameters are fitted by maximum likelihood (as scipy.stats fit(): mean and standard deviation with divisor n; minimum and mean minus minimum; minimum and range) to the first reference_size observations, and again after every drift.

m

Number of buckets of the sketch (the memory units of the paper).

alpha

Significance level: drift when the p-value is <= alpha.

grace_period

Number of observations processed before the test is applied (the paper tests once more observations than memory units were seen; the default is m). It counts from the start of the sketch, so with a fitted distribution it includes the reference observations.

reference_size

With a fitted distribution (cdf a name), the number of observations it is fitted to. They are also the first observations of the sketch, as in the call-center experiment of the paper.

exact

Exact distribution of the statistic (TRUE, the default, as the reference code) or the limiting distribution (FALSE); see ks_sf().

min_instances

Passed to greedyks().

target_feat

Feature to be monitored.

Value

dfr_greedyks object

Details

After a drift, the sketch restarts empty (and, with a fitted distribution, the reference is fitted again to the next reference_size observations).

The output of each observation (drifter_output after fit()) has the estimated statistic D and its p-value p_value. For speed, when more than 140 observations were processed and n D^2 < 2.2, the p-value is the Pelz-Good approximation instead of the exact Durbin matrix (its p-value there is above 0.02); with alpha >= 0.02 the exact value is used. The decisions are those of the exact test.

References

Cardoso, D. O. and Galeno, T. D. (2023). Online evaluation of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test on arbitrarily large samples. Journal of Computational Science, 67, 101959. doi:10.1016/j.jocs.2023.101959

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)
set.seed(1)
x <- c(rnorm(1000, 1, 1), rnorm(4000, 1.3, 1))
detector <- fit(dfr_greedyks(cdf = function(q) pnorm(q, 1, 1)), x)
which(detector$drifter_output$drift)
#>  [1] 1534 1636 1742 1846 2169 2291 2392 2493 2689 2790 2891 2992 3093 3194 3296
#> [16] 3397 3512 3704 3855 3962 4094 4214 4338 4439 4622 4723 4824
# reference fitted to the first 300 observations
detector <- fit(dfr_greedyks(cdf = "norm", reference_size = 300), x)
which(detector$drifter_output$drift)
#> [1] 1534 4654
